The National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) was founded on September 22, 1910, by Justo Sierra, aiming to create a secular, national institution distinct from the 19th-century Royal and Pontifical University of Mexico. The university unified various colleges of higher education in Mexico City to reorganize the country's higher education system. Initially, it faced significant political challenges due to the Mexican Revolution and federal government control, leading to student strikes and a temporary split with the law faculty. The university operates over 324,000 students across multiple campuses in Mexico City and throughout Mexico, including specialized campuses in Querétaro, Morelia, and Mérida, as well as extension schools in the United States and Canada. It is recognized as one of the most international research universities in Latin America, with Nobel laureates Alfonso García Robles, Octavio Paz, and Mario Molina among its alumni.
